title: Localization preserves morphisms out of a left orthogonal object
statement: Let $\mathcal T$ be a triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category] and $\mathcal E$ a strictly full triangulated subcategory [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]. Let $W_{\mathcal E}$ be the class of morphisms $u:X\to Y$ for which there is a distinguished triangle $X\xrightarrow{u}Y\to Z\to X[1]$ with $Z\in\mathcal E$. Let $\mathcal D$ be a category and $L:\mathcal T\to\mathcal D$ a localization at $W_{\mathcal E}$: $L$ inverts these morphisms, and for every category $\mathcal B$, precomposition by $L$ is an equivalence from $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal D,\mathcal B)$ onto the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal T,\mathcal B)$ consisting of functors inverting $W_{\mathcal E}$. Enlarge the universe for these functor categories as needed. Let $P\in\mathcal T$ satisfy $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(P,E)=0$ for every $E\in\mathcal E$; this condition is called left orthogonality to $\mathcal E$. Then for every $N\in\mathcal T$ the canonical map $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(P,N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(LP,LN)$ sending $f$ to $L(f)$ is bijective. No boundedness, compactness or coproduct hypothesis is imposed.
